## Exciting News: New Content Types Now Available on Zenith Community!

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ000009yj3V0AQ/exciting-news-new-content-types-now-available-on-zenith-community
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-01-27T14:49:53.000Z

Article Details

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

January 27, 2025 at 2:49 PM

Exciting News: New Content Types Now Available on Zenith Community!

Hello Zenith Community,

Over the past year, we’ve seen incredible growth and engagement following our transition to the new platform. This move has been instrumental in enhancing our community strategy and aligning more closely with our company’s broader vision.

While the transition has brought many benefits, we’ve also recognized the challenges some of you have faced—particularly with character limitations and the types of content you could share.

We’re thrilled to announce that starting today, new content types are now available to our members! This update empowers you to share a richer variety of content, beyond just questions. You’ll now have the ability to create blogs, guides, articles, and more—complete with rich media and extended character limits. Whether you want to share in-depth insights, step-by-step guides, or thought-provoking blogs, the possibilities are now greater than ever.

Here’s how it works:

Silver II members and above can create:

Blogs

Guides

Questions

Copper II members and above can create:

Blogs

Questions

Copper I members and new joiners can:

Post new questions and replies

This tiered approach ensures that as you grow within the community, new opportunities to share and engage unlock.

We’re excited to see how these new content types will inspire deeper conversations, greater collaboration, and more knowledge sharing across our vibrant community.

Thank you for being an essential part of the Zenith Community.

## Understanding Reputation in the Zenith Community

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000AqEPJ0A3/understanding-reputation-in-the-zenith-community
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-02-28T17:03:53.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

February 28, 2025 at 5:03 PM

Understanding Reputation in the Zenith Community

The Zenith Community thrives on collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and engagement. To recognize and reward contributions, we use a reputation system. As you participate, you earn reputation points, unlocking new capabilities and privileges within the community.

Reputation Levels

Reputation grows over time, and as you accumulate points, you progress through the following levels:

Copper I

Copper II

Bronze I

Bronze II

Silver I

Silver II

Gold I

Gold II

Platinum I

Platinum II

Diamond

Champion

Our

Leaderboards

highlight top members who have earned the most reputation, showcasing their contributions to the community.

Earning Reputation

You can earn reputation points by actively engaging in the community through various actions, including:

Writing a post

– Share your insights and experiences.

Liking content

– Show appreciation for valuable contributions.

Receiving likes

– Get recognition for your posts.

Answering questions

– Help others by sharing your expertise.

Having your answer marked as the best

– Provide top-quality solutions.

Other engagement activities

– Various tasks contribute to your reputation growth over time.

Content Types & Access Levels

As your reputation increases, you unlock access to different types of content creation.

Silver II members and above

can create:

Blogs

Guides

Questions

Copper II members and above

can create:

Blogs

Questions

Copper I members and new joiners

can:

Post new questions and replies

This tiered access system ensures that high-quality content is produced and shared within the community.

Reputation Moderation

When you first join the community, your posts will be held for review. This helps us ensure posts are placed in the right sections and do not contain sensitive data. While this may seem like an extra step, it helps maintain content quality and accuracy.

Once you

earn 400 points and move past Copper I

, your posts will no longer require moderation.

Grow Your Reputation, Expand Your Influence

Reputation in the Zenith Community is more than just points—it represents your contributions, expertise, and engagement. As you climb the ranks, you gain greater influence and the ability to contribute more valuable content.

## Accessibility Enhancements Launching This Saturday!

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000DyzNh0AJ/accessibility-enhancements-launching-this-saturday
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-07-09T16:00:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

July 9, 2025 at 4:00 PM

Accessibility Enhancements Launching This Saturday!

We’re very happy to be rolling out a set of major accessibility improvements this Saturday (07/12/2025), which is something that’s been on our roadmap for a while now. We wanted to make sure these changes interoperated with our customizations before releasing, and we're happy to say we have arrived!

Here’s what’s coming:

Screen Reader Compatibility – Most UI components now offer better support for screen readers.

Keyboard Navigation – Static content is now fully navigable using arrow keys.

Improved Contrast Ratios – Text is easier to read with updated color contrast that meets WCAG guidelines.

Descriptive Labels – Buttons and form fields are now clearly labeled for assistive technologies.

Focus Indicators – It's now easy to see which element is selected when tabbing through the interface.

This is a foundational update to up-level our inclusivity and compliance with accessibility standards, all while retaining the customized experience we have worked to deliver.

We're excited to launch these ADA features and we hope you are as well!

Ramesh Mani

## Customer Support Portal (CSP) Access FAQ

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000Ez8jl0AB/customer-support-portal-csp-access-faq
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2026-05-18T14:57:16.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited May 18, 2026 at 2:57 PM

Customer Support Portal (CSP) Access FAQ

This FAQ addresses common questions regarding accessing the Zscaler Customer Support Portal (CSP) and creating support cases, in light of the deprecation of the Public Case submission forms.

1. Why is the Public Case submission form being deprecated?

The Public Case form is being deprecated to streamline the support process and encourage customers to utilize the Customer Support Portal (CSP) for all support related activities. This ensures a more efficient, and comprehensive support experience with enhanced tracking and access to technical resources.

2. How can I access the Customer Support Portal (CSP)?

There are two primary ways to access the Customer Support Portal (CSP):

Option 1: Accessing the CSP from the Product UI

Zscaler provides direct links to the CSP within its product user interfaces for convenience.

Locate the Support Link:

Within your Zscaler product UI (e.g., ZIA, ZPA, ZDX), look for a "Help"/ “?” icon .

Click to Access CSP:

Clicking this link shows the “Submit a Ticket”/ “Get Support” option which will redirect you to the Zscaler CSP. Examples below :

Option 2: Accessing CSP via the Zscaler Zenith Community

The Zscaler Zenith Community is a place for Zscaler customers, users, and partners to collaborate, learn, and share knowledge about Zscaler's products and zero trust security. The Community also provides an alternate login option to CSP

Navigate to the Zscaler Zenith Community:

Go to the Zscaler Zenith Community homepage.

Member Login:

Click on the "Member Login" button and enter your Zscaler registered email address and password.

Access Customer Support Portal Option:

Once logged into Zenith, look for the "Resources" section, then click on the "Customer Support Portal" option.

Authenticated Login :

An email-based authentication check is done before logging into the Customer Support Portal (CSP ).

3. What if I am a first-time user of the Zscaler Zenith Community?

If you are new to the Zscaler Zenith Community, you will need to complete a one-time registration process.

Access the Registration Page:

On the Zscaler Zenith Community homepage, locate and click the "Register" option.

Provide Required Information:

Fill in the essential details, including your corporate email address (registered with Zscaler), first name, last name, company name, job title, and country.

Important:

To access the Customer Support Portal from within Zenith Community, you must use an email address registered with Zscaler. Users registered with a personal email address can only access the Zenith Community. If you are not registered with Zscaler, please contact your administrator.

Create a Password:

Set a strong unique password.

Agree to Terms and Conditions:

Review and accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Email Verification:

A verification email will be sent to your registered email address. Click the verification link to confirm your email.

After successful verification, you will receive a "Create Password" email, and subsequently be directed to Zenith Community access.

4. How do I create a new case once logged into the Customer Support Portal (CSP)?

Once you have successfully logged into the CSP:

Locate "Create a Case" Button:

Look for a “+New Ticket” to initiate case creation. This is found on the main dashboard or navigation menu.

Select Case Type:

You may be prompted to select a case type (Problem, Questions, Provisioning, or Categorization). Choose the most relevant option.

Fill Out the Other Relevant Fields.

Self-Help Docs: During the case creation process, concise self-help documents can assist you to get more information about the issue/problem you may be encountering.

Submit Case:

Review the provided information and click the "Submit Case" button.

5. What if I encounter login issues?

Incorrect Credentials:

Ensure you are using your Zscaler registered email address and password.

Non-Registered Email:

If you are trying to access CSP with an email address not registered with Zscaler, or if your ZIA/ZPA/ZDX user information is not found, you will receive an error message. To access the CSP, your email address must be registered with Zscaler.

Not Logged In:

If you attempt to connect to the CSP without being logged into Zenith, you will be prompted to log in first.

If you continue to experience admin login difficulties, please contact your Zscaler administrator for assistance or reach out to Zscaler

support

## Important Update: Public Case Submission Forms Decommissioning

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000Ez8lN0AR/important-update-public-case-submission-forms-decommissioning
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-08-15T12:45:52.000Z

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

August 15, 2025 at 12:45 PM

Important Update: Public Case Submission Forms Decommissioning

Effective August 15, 2025, Zscaler will be Decommissioning the Public Case Submission Forms.

This means:

Support tickets must now be submitted through the Customer Support Portal (CSP).

Impacted Users:

Anyone who previously used the Public Case Form will need to switch to the CSP for creating support cases.

Your Next Steps:

Please submit all future support requests via the CSP accessible within the Zscaler product or from the Zenith Community. The CSP offers a more efficient and trackable case management experience.

For additional questions or assistance, contact Zscaler Support via the Product Portal or visit the Resources section of our Community.

For more information, please see the FAQ

Gianluca.bastia

(Partner)

11 months ago

What is the guidance to partners that have access to multiple tenants with the same email address?

I currently get an error when trying to access the CSP and have only been able to use the forms to submit tickets.

Ben_Garrison

(Partner)

11 months ago

Just to close this loop as I’m aware your question has been answered privately.

Zscaler permits the management of customer tenants by our partners through MSSP program . MSSP authorised partners are provided access to Support Portal for Partners (SPP), which allows the management of cases across multiple customer accounts and tenants.

Zscaler Certifications Now Recognized by ISC2 | Accelerate your path to CISSP

For professionals pursuing their CISSP certification, Zscaler is proud to announce that the ZDTA, ZDTE, and ZDXA certifications are now officially recognized by ISC2.

Effective now,

these certifications will count as

experience waivers

toward the CISSP’s professional experience requirement, recognizing the depth and relevance of Zscaler’s programs in advancing global cybersecurity skills.

The CISSP, established in 1994, remains one of the world’s most respected information security credentials, held by more than 165,000 professionals worldwide. This new recognition underscores the shared commitment of Zscaler and ISC2 to strengthen the cybersecurity talent pool with modern cloud security expertise.

We are doing something better than we did before because of your efforts. I hope we can do something more to promote this relationship. I really appreciate all you have done.

— Casey Marks, Chief Operating Officer, ISC2

## Domain Reclassification Requests on Community

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000GeEXh0AN/domain-reclassification-requests-on-community
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-11-24T14:57:16.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited November 24, 2025 at 2:57 PM

Domain Reclassification Requests on Community

Hey everyone,

We’ve noticed an increase in posts requesting domain reclassification or recategorization, so I wanted to provide some clarity on how this process works and what options are available.

Every Zscaler customer manages their own access policies, including which site categories are allowed or blocked. For example, if an organization chooses to block the MISC category, then any site classified under MISC will be blocked according to their policy. Newly created domains are also automatically categorized, which is often where these questions come up.

If You Are a Zscaler Customer

You can use the

Site Review

page to see how a domain is currently categorized and submit a reclassification request if needed. This is the recommended and supported path.

If You Are Not a Zscaler Customer

But your company works with a mutual customer who is reporting that your domain is being blocked:

You can ask your customer to check the Site Review page to confirm the category and, if appropriate, submit a recategorization request on their side.

If that’s not an ideal approach for your situation, your other option is to contact

Zscaler Support

to see whether they can assist with a review. Please note that support cannot guarantee a recategorization, but it is the formal channel available.

A Quick Note About Community Posts

Community members and moderators do not have the ability to change domain categories. Because of this, posts requesting recategorization will be removed; not to dismiss the issue, but because the community cannot take action on these requests.

If you’re experiencing domain categorization challenges, please use the official channels above so your request is routed to the right team.

Thanks for your understanding, and we hope this helps clear up the process!

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000GeFTl0AN/worth-the-read-embedded-ai","lastmod":"2025-12-19T14:17:33.000Z","id":"aSmPJ00000GeFTl0AN"} -->
## Worth the read - Embedded AI

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000GeFTl0AN/worth-the-read-embedded-ai
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-12-19T14:17:33.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Certification

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited December 19, 2025 at 2:17 PM

Worth the read - Embedded AI

I just read this blog post that Steve Grossenbacher

published regarding AI being embedded and hidden in line of business applications, (Jira, Slack, Copilot etc). I wasn't really shocked to see that we have seen a 36x increase in transactions year-over-year, but what did catch my attention is how fundamentally different this problem is from the shadow AI we were dealing with a year ago.

Back then, you could block ChatGPT and move on. Now? Every app your employees rely on has AI baked in, and each one is quietly talking to different LLMs under different terms.

He goes on to say that over 40% of enterprise AI usage is now this embedded AI, and it's mostly operating in the blind. Traditional DLP doesn't catch it because the interaction happens inside trusted apps. Steve also mentions that Microsoft Copilot is probably the most extreme example, as it has access to your entire M365 Graph; one careless prompt could exfiltrate basically anything.

Check out the blog post

and let me know your thoughts. Should be interesting to see how our

upcoming AI innovations

address this, it definitely feels like the right problem to be solving.

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

January 7, 2026 at 5:39 PM

Search Functionality Upgrade

We will be upgrading our search functionality framework on 10th January as part of our ongoing efforts to improve platform performance and user experience. This upgrade will enhance search result load times and deliver a more optimized and seamless experience for our users.

During the upgrade window, you may experience intermittent issues while fetching search results. If this occurs, a simple page refresh should resolve the issue and display the results as expected. Thank you for your understanding and continued support.

johnsonto

(Customer)

6 months ago

Thank you for the heads up.

## 📢 Certification Authorization to Test – Important Update

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000GeKWf0AN/-certification-authorization-to-test-important-update
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2026-04-07T16:15:47.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Certification

Rohini Balmiki

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited April 7, 2026 at 4:15 PM

📢 Certification Authorization to Test – Important Update

On February 1, 2026, we officially removed prerequisite requirements for our globally offered certifications: ZDTA, ZDTE, and ZDXA.

🎯 What’s changed?

All Zscaler Cyber Academy candidates are now eligible to sit for any of these exams—no prerequisites required! While training courses and associated labs are no longer mandatory, they are still highly recommended to help you prepare.

📩 Why did you receive an email?

You may have received an “Authorization to Test” email from Pearson VUE (our exam delivery partner). These notifications were automatically sent to all users with a Zscaler Cyber Academy account as part of this update.

✅ What this means for you:

- You are now eligible to schedule any of the ZDTA, ZDTE, or ZDXA exams

- No prior certifications or prerequisites are required

- You can take the exam whenever you're ready

⏳ Not planning to test right now?

No problem—you can safely ignore these emails. We apologize for any confusion caused.

🔄 Additional info:

- All new Zscaler Cyber Academy accounts will automatically receive exam eligibility going forward

We’re excited to make our certification program more accessible and flexible for everyone.

Article Details

Certification

Rohini Balmiki

(Employee) posted an Article

April 7, 2026 at 3:08 PM

📢 Certification Authorization to Test – Important Update

On February 1, 2026, we officially removed prerequisite requirements for our globally offered certifications: ZDTA, ZDTE, and ZDXA.

🎯 What’s changed?

All Zscaler Cyber Academy candidates are now eligible to sit for any of these exams—no prerequisites required! While training courses and associated labs are no longer mandatory, they are still highly recommended to help you prepare.

📩 Why did you receive an email?

You may have received an “Authorization to Test” email from Pearson VUE (our exam delivery partner). These notifications were automatically sent to all users with a Zscaler Cyber Academy account as part of this update.

✅ What this means for you:

- You are now eligible to schedule any of the ZDTA, ZDTE, or ZDXA exams

- No prior certifications or prerequisites are required

- You can take the exam whenever you're ready

⏳ Not planning to test right now?

No problem—you can safely ignore these emails. We apologize for any confusion caused.

🔄 Additional info:

- All new Zscaler Cyber Academy accounts will automatically receive exam eligibility going forward

We’re excited to make our certification program more accessible and flexible for everyone.

Richard Hesselbach

(Employee)

3 months ago

The removal of the pre-requirements aligns Zscaler with other industry certification players in that if you are knowledgeable enough and have enough hands-on experience there is no need to attend the trainings and pass other exams in order to get certified on your desired platform (ZDTA/ZDTE/ZDXA). (EX: Cisco CCNA).

Although the requirement has been removed it is still highly recommended that you attend the Associated Trainings and the recommended Zscaler Training Path for maximum understanding.

Alejandro Knudsen

(Employee) posted an Article

May 20, 2026 at 4:34 PM

Completed ZTCA or EDU‑104? Your next no-cost, step before EDU‑200 Lab

If you’ve already completed Zero Trust Cyber Associate (ZTCA) eLearning and/or Mastering the Fundamentals of Zero Trust (EDU‑104), you’ve built a strong foundation. Now it’s time to turn that knowledge into repeatable, day-to-day workflows.

If you haven’t enrolled in or completed Zscaler for Users – Administrator (EDU‑200) Lab yet, here’s a great next move: Introduction to Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (EDU‑100) Workshop, available as a no-cost offering on Zscaler Cyber Academy.

Why EDU‑100 works as a bridge

Introduction to Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (EDU‑100) Workshop helps you build minimum viable operational competency through guided, hands-on simulations aligned to a targeted subset of Zscaler for Users – Administrator (EDU‑200) Lab activities. You can practice key tasks first, then step into the lab experience with more confidence.

And because it’s simulation-based, you can get hands-on practice without a dedicated lab tenant, using guided exercises you can return to for reinforcement.

How to enroll / access

Get started here:

Customer

Partner

Session dates

Introduction to Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (EDU-100) Workshop is delivered as two (2) live webinars (4 hours each; 8 hours total). Choose your region:

APJ: May 21 and May 22, 2026

EMEA: May 18 and May 19, 2026

AMS: May 27 and May 28, 2026

Have you already completed ZTCA eLearning or EDU‑104 and are you planning to take the no-cost EDU‑100 Workshop next?

Community Highlights

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted an Article

May 26, 2026 at 6:13 PM

How to Use Filtering and Sorting in the Activity Widget

Hello,

Just wanted to stop in with a refresh on how to use the activity widget on the homepage. I never like to assume that things are self-explanatory so here is a brief recap on how to use the activity widget filters and sorting on the main page.

Sort by content type:

Posts – Community questions and discussions

Blogs – Longer-form thought leadership and idea sharing

Articles – Technical guides, newsletters, and other resources

Events – Available on the dedicated

Events page

Filter by status:

Answered - Has replies but no marked solution

Unanswered - No replies at all

Solved - When an author of a question marks an answer as best answer

Sort by:

Recent Activity – Recent likes, comments, or interactions push content to the top

Latest – Newest published content first

Top – Most engaged content based on views, likes, and comments

These tools make it easier to find the most relevant content and stay up to date with what’s happening in the community.

Alejandro Knudsen

(Employee) posted an Article

June 9, 2026 at 5:43 PM

ZLive26 Day 1 Recap: Training and Certification Happy Hour Takes the Spotlight

Day 1 is officially in the books—and Zenith Live 26 came out swinging. From the first sessions of the day, the energy was clear: Zenith Community members showed up ready to learn, compare notes, and leave with practical takeaways they can apply back at work.

Monday’s theme: hands-on learning and next steps

If Day 1 had one headline, it was training. Conversations across the event kept circling back to the same priorities:

How do I level up my skills in a way that actually sticks?

What should I learn next based on my role and current responsibilities?

What’s the clearest path from foundational Zero Trust concepts to hands-on implementation?

What we heard from the community

Throughout the day, members weren’t just looking for updates—they were looking for direction: which sessions to prioritize, what to take next, and how to turn learning into repeatable workflows.

Exciting activities we have planned

If you’re onsite, we’ve got exciting activities planned and we’d love to connect—whether you’re looking to validate your learning path, talk through certification options, or just meet other practitioners and swap stories from the field.

A Day 1 highlight was our Certifications Happy Hour on Monday afternoon—a great opportunity to engage with our Champions, swap stories from the field, and connect around what’s next in training and certifications. Thanks to our sponsor SecureDynamics

If you walked away with a clearer plan (or even just one key insight you can use immediately), that’s a strong Day 1 win.

If you’re here in person…

Come say hello and bring your questions—especially if you’re mapping out training, preparing for a certification, or aligning learning goals across your team. We’re happy to help you build a plan that fits your role, timeline, and priorities.

Rohini Balmiki

(Employee) posted a Blog

January 7, 2026 at 3:59 PM

🚀 New Year, New Cert: Get Zscaler Certified for only $75!

Start the year by boosting your career journey and validating your expertise in cloud security. For a limited time, we’re offering a 75% discount on select Zscaler Certification Exams!

The Offer:

Get your ZDTA, ZDTE, or ZDXA certification exam for just $75 (regularly $300).

How to Claim Your Discount:

To ensure a smooth registration process, please follow these steps:

1️⃣ Start in the Academy:

https://lnkd.in/g2UPFJyM

2️⃣ Complete Prerequisites: Ensure you have finished the required learning modules. You must complete the coursework to unlock the exam registration link.

3️⃣ Book via Pearson VUE: Once your learning is complete, keep an eye out for an email containing your ZCID. This email will guide you on how to create your account with our delivery partner, Pearson VUE, so you can schedule your exam.

4️⃣ Apply Code at Checkout: Use promo code NewYearCertz on the payment screen to redeem your discount.

The Fine Print:

Deadline: Exams must be scheduled and completed by January 31, 2026.

Exclusions: This offer does not apply to Hands-On Labs or the ZTCA exam.

Partners: Note that Partners already receive their best available pricing via the Partner Portal.

Whether you're looking to advance your career or strengthen your Zero Trust knowledge, now is the perfect time to make it happen. The clock is ticking, finish your learning and book your seat today!

## Joy to Recognition: Certification Champion Spotlight with Manuel Bock

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Blogs/aSnPJ0000000dsb0AA/joy-to-recognition-certification-champion-spotlight-with-manuel-bock
- Type: Blog
- Last activity: 2026-07-24T19:38:55.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Blog Details

Certification

Alejandro Knudsen

(Employee) posted a Blog

5m ago

Joy to Recognition: Certification Champion Spotlight with Manuel Bock

Manuel Bock, Head of IT at

infinit.cx

, approaches learning with a mindset that’s both practical and refreshingly honest. For him, certifications are the fastest short track to gaining real knowledge. Rather than chasing badges for their own sake, he’s used Zscaler credentials as a structured way to build understanding quickly, especially early on, when he was still developing his foundation.

Manuel’s journey began with the Zero Trust Cyber Associate (ZTCA), a key milestone that helped him establish strong Zero Trust fundamentals and gave him a clear starting point for deeper learning. From there, he expanded his expertise with additional legacy Zscaler certificates, including ZIA Certified Administrator, ZPA Certified Administrator, and the Zscaler Cloud Transformation Specialist (ZCTS) certificate. Together, these credentials helped him strengthen the practical knowledge he relies on day to day.

The biggest value, Manuel says, is how this learning helped him understand how Zscaler works under the hood. It also helped him learn the specific wording and terminology Zscaler uses, which can make a real difference when you’re operating, troubleshooting, or explaining concepts to others. He notes that earning these credentials also opened access to earlier community learning environments, which supported his continued growth.

When asked which credential was most challenging, Manuel points back to a moment many learners recognize immediately. The first one. Not because the content was impossible, but because he “had yet no extensive knowledge of Zscaler” at the time. That first step became the turning point, because once you begin, each next step builds on the last.

Manuel is also candid about the career impact. He views credentials as an add on in the broader professional picture, but still an important one, especially for visibility on platforms like LinkedIn and at community events. In other words, the badge can help you get noticed, but the knowledge is what helps you deliver.

His proudest moment, however, wasn’t a score report. It was recognition. Manuel recalls the first time he learned he would be one of very few Zscaler Trailblazers, and then seeing his name appear on the Community/Cyber Academy “Wall of Fame” at Zenith Live in Berlin. For him, it was a clear signal that consistency, learning, and participation don’t go unnoticed.

When it comes to learning support, Manuel credits the Zenith Community in the best way possible. The people. Over time, a few connections even became real friendships he meets regularly outside of work. As for what helped most, he points to the old community forum and a privately organized weekly Zscaler Community call with Zscaler admins across the DACH region, spanning both some of the largest and smallest companies. It’s a reminder that sometimes the most valuable study resource is simply staying close to practitioners who are solving similar challenges.

Looking ahead, Manuel plans to recertify and or update his existing credentials this year, and he hopes to intensify his community engagement again, especially if there’s a stronger community focused platform experience. Next on his roadmap is the new Zscaler for Users Engineer (ZDTE).

As a Cyber Academy Certification Champion, Manuel says he feels “very honored and proud,” and is thankful to Zscaler for paving the road and for the opportunity to be featured in this spotlight again. His advice to anyone considering their first step is simple and direct. “Just start. The better you get, the easier the next step.”

In one word, Manuel sums it all up. Joy.

Words of Wisdom from Manuel Bock

Start with strong fundamentals. Manuel’s journey began with ZTCA, building a solid Zero Trust base to grow from.

Use certificates to go deeper. His ZIA and ZPA Administrator certificates and ZCTS certificate helped him build practical, job relevant understanding.

The first step is the hardest. Starting without deep product experience is often the biggest hurdle. After that, progress accelerates.

Learn the platform language. Understanding how Zscaler works under the hood, and how it’s described, makes you more effective.

Just start, then keep going. “The better you get, the easier is the next step.”

Learning goes further with other learners. Introduce yourself in the comments and share your role, region, and the certification you’re aiming for next.

## How to Access Your Cases in the Zscaler Customer Support Portal

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000005aCX0AY/how-to-access-your-cases-in-the-zscaler-customer-support-portal
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2025-09-25T16:40:36.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Ankita Patel

(Employee) posted a Guide

September 25, 2025 at 4:40 PM

How to Access Your Cases in the Zscaler Customer Support Portal

The support case management dashboard available on the Home page gives you a concise view of your recently created/updated cases.

1. Click on

“View All”

to view or update all the cases associated with your account.

You can view cases based on the folders provided:

Pending Action:

All cases with any action pending from your end would be visible here

My Open Cases:

All cases opened by you as a requester would reflect here

All Open Cases:

All cases associated with your account will be visible here

Closed Cases:

All the closed cases of an account are enlisted here

Note:

The default view is

“All Open Cases”.

You can click on the other folders to view the cases under them.

2. You can further filter out cases from the selected folder by searching using the case number, requestor or any keyword. There are added filters such as

“Product”

and

“Date”

to narrow down your search.

3. Click on

“Export”

to download your cases in a .csv file.

## Building a new Nanolog Streaming Service server and duplicating the log feeds

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000005maH0AQ/building-a-new-nanolog-streaming-service-server-and-duplicating-the-log-feeds
- Type: Guide

- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

This page has an error. You might just need to refresh it.

Error during LWC component connect phase: [Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'substring')]

Technical Guides

Arusch317

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 25, 2026 at 1:32 PM

Building a new Nanolog Streaming Service server and duplicating the log feeds

If you need to rebuild your Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) server you can back up custom configuration files, and copy your existing feeds to avoid any interruption in log streaming. The following procedure shows you how to backup essential files in your existing NSS server and copy your NSS feeds:

Step 1: Backup files from existing NSS server, if required

Connect to NSS server via Secure Copy Protocol (SCP) and download:

/etc/rc.conf

If you have manually configured routes, back up this file. If not, this is not required.

/etc/ntp.conf

If you have manually configured a specific Network Time Protocol (NTP) server, back up this file. If your server uses the native NTP server from Linux, this is not required.

/etc/snmpd.conf

If you have configured Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) on the existing NSS server, back up this file. If not, this is not required.

Note: On the existing NSS server, run the command crontab -l to verify if you have configured any cron jobs. If so, back up the output and duplicate the job in the new NSS server.

Step 2: Prepare the New NSS Server

Access Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) Configuration

In the ZIA Admin Portal, go to Administration > Nanolog Streaming Service.

Add a New NSS Server

Select Add NSS Server and fill out the required fields:

Name: Enter a recognizable name for the new NSS server (e.g., Test 2).

Type: Choose the NSS type (e.g., NSS for Web).

Status: Ensure it is set to Enabled.

Deploy the NSS server

Deploy the virtual appliance with the NSS image as per your preferred platform (OVA, ISO, etc.).For detailed instructions on how to deploy NSS please refer to the Help

here

If you have any customer configuration files from the old NSS server, copy them to the new server in the same location using SCP.

Ensure the newly deployed NSS connects successfully to your environment and appears healthy in the portal.

Note: Ensure that firewalls and your Security Incident and Event Management Monitoring (SIEM) are configured to allow traffic from the new NSS server IP.

Step 3: Copy Existing Feeds to the New NSS

Review and Copy Existing Feeds

In the existing feeds list, click

Copy

on the desired feed to duplicate the feed.

Give a name to the newly copied feed:

In the newly copied feed, select the new NSS Server deployed in Step 1 from the NSS Server drop-down

Validate the settings from the old feed, including:

Status

SIEM Destination Type, SIEM TCP Port, and IP Address/FQDN

Log Type, Feed Output Type, and Feed Output Format

Filters

Step 4: Validate Connectivity to the SIEM

Verify Feed Status

Navigate to NSS Feeds in the portal. Confirm:

Both the old and new feeds are listed as Enabled , showing active feeds for both old and new NSS servers).

Validate Logs in the SIEM

Check your SIEM for logs arriving from the new NSS server. Ensure:

Filters and parsing rules are applied as expected.

If you observe duplications, this is expected as both the old and new feeds are sent during validation. It will stop once the old feed is deleted in Step 5.

If you want to to see the exact index time of the active feeds, you can use this command on the NSS server:

"/sc/bin/smmgr -g clt_cur_datatime -j feed -d stats"

Step 5: Finalize the Migration

4.1 Deactivate and Remove the Old NSS Feed

After validating that the new feed is logging to your SIEM, you can disable and remove the old feed associated with the legacy NSS server.

Return to the NSS Feeds page, locate the old feed, and select Delete.

Decommission the old NSS server

Once all old feeds are removed, safely decommission the legacy NSS server in your environment. You don’t have to delete the old NSS server right away, we recommend waiting at least 48 hours to validate that the new NSS server is stable.

Power down the old server.

Update any related documentation to reflect the new NSS server configuration.

## Excluding an admin's name from PDF exports in Web Insights

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000063sr0AA/excluding-an-admins-name-from-pdf-exports-in-web-insights
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-06T20:27:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 6, 2026 at 8:27 PM

Excluding an admin's name from PDF exports in Web Insights

Note:

Special thanks to

Aishwarya H T

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction:

This article explains the available options for removing an administrator's name from Portable Document Format (PDF) exports generated via Web Insights. By design, Web Insights includes the admin's name or login ID in the header or footer of all PDF exports. Currently, there is no built-in setting within the ZIA Admin Portal to disable this feature.

Solution:

However, you can use the following workarounds to remove this information:

Edit the PDF after downloading

: After downloading the report, you can use a PDF editing tool, such as Adobe Acrobat's Redact tool, to manually remove the admin's name from the header or footer before sharing the document.

Export to CSV

: Export the report data as a Comma-Separated Values (CSV) file. Open the file, delete the column or fields that contain the admin identifier, and then save the file. If a PDF is required, you can then convert the modified CSV file to a PDF.

Use the browser's print function

: Some web browsers offer a "Print to PDF" option that might allow you to hide page headers and footers in the print preview setting. Review the preview carefully to confirm that the admin identifier is not included before generating the PDF.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

## How to enforce IP protection for the ZIdentity Admin Portal?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ000000642X0AQ/how-to-enforce-ip-protection-for-the-zidentity-admin-portal
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-06T20:26:58.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 6, 2026 at 8:26 PM

How to enforce IP protection for the ZIdentity Admin Portal?

Note:

Special thanks to

Zain Rafiqi

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction:

Ensuring that only authorized team members can access your administrative settings is a vital part of maintaining a secure environment. Zscaler Identity (ZIdentity) provides a way to restrict access to the ZIdentity Admin Portal based on a user's source Internet Protocol (IP) address. By defining trusted locations, you can make sure your portal remains protected from unauthorized access attempts.

Administrators may need to limit access to the ZIdentity Admin Portal to specific office branches or secure networks. Without these restrictions, the portal might be accessible from any Internet Protocol (IP) address, which increases the risk of unauthorized login attempts from untrusted locations.

Solution:

Enforcing IP protection is a straightforward process that involves two primary phases: identifying your trusted locations and then creating a policy to enforce those boundaries.

Part 1: Define Trusted IP Locations

First, you must identify and register the IP addresses or ranges used by your authorized personnel.

Log in to the

ZIdentity Admin Portal

Navigate to

Administration

Security

IP Locations

Click Add

Location

Name: Enter a descriptive name for the location (e.g. Srinagar_Office_Range).

Country: Select the country associated with the IP range.

IP Address: Enter the public IP address or a CIDR range (e.g., 1.2.3.4 or 1.2.3.0/24).

Click Update to save and validate the location.

Part 2: Configure the Admin Single Sign-On Policy

After the locations are defined, you must create a rule that evaluates these locations during the login process.

Navigate to

Policy

Admin Sign-On

Click

Add Rule

Rule Name: Provide a name (e.g., Restrict_to_OnSite_Locations).

Rule Status: Ensure the status is set to Enabled

Criteria: Select the conditions for the rule. Please see the screenshot for example below.

Action: Select

Allow or Deny

Click

Save

to validate the rule

Note

: The default rule (not displayed) is set to allow all, so it is better to create blocking rules.

For example, create this rule to prevent administrators from connecting from an IP that is not in the range of the On-Site location:

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

## How to configure a secondary IdP for vendors without impacting internal users

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000064Lt0AI/how-to-configure-a-secondary-idp-for-vendors-without-impacting-internal-users
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-06T20:26:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 6, 2026 at 8:26 PM

How to configure a secondary IdP for vendors without impacting internal users

Note:

Special thanks to Prabhjot Singh for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction:

If internal users require the User Principal Name (UPN) and vendors require the 'user.mail' attribute for authentication (due to UPN changes for guest users in Azure), altering the SAML NameID attribute to 'user.mail' on the production Identity Provider (IDP) will negatively affect internal users whose UPN and 'user.mail' values differ.

Consequently, it is advisable to configure a distinct secondary IDP exclusively for vendors to ensure internal user authentication remains unaffected.

Solution:

To configure a secondary IdP for vendors, please follow the steps below:

Set up the new IDP configurations in Azure, refer to the documentation

Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On

for more details.

After successfully setting up the new SAML application in Azure, in step 6(c) of the following documentation,

Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On

, navigate to

Single Sign-On settings

for the app and click

Edit

in the

Attributes & Claims section

Update the NameID to "user.mail" to ensure consistency across SAML and SCIM.

In

Advanced Settings

, edit the

Advanced SAML Claims

options, and ensure you select the checkbox "

Append application ID to issuer

Complete the steps up to step 7 as mentioned in the following documentation:

Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-on

Important Additional Steps:

Download the metadata file of your Azure application.

Before uploading the metadata to the ZPA admin portal, append the Azure Application ID to the entityID in the metadata file:

Go to the Overview section of your Azure application and copy the Application ID.

Open the metadata file using a text editor, locate the entityID attribute, append the application ID, and save the file.

Upload this modified metadata file to the ZPA admin portal when creating the new IdP configuration.

Enable SCIM

and provision the necessary vendor-specific users to the new Vendor ZPA enterprise application.

On the

ZPA admin portal

under the new Vendor IDP configurations, make sure to enable "

Use with Arbitrary Domains"

Note

: If the "

Use with Arbitrary Domains

" feature is enabled for the

primary

internal

IdP

, all authentication requests will be routed to the primary IdP, which will not resolve our purpose. Hence, ensure this feature is only enabled for the secondary or Vendor-specific IdP, so that the requests for vendors will route through secondary IdP.

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

## Bypass authentication for specific destinations only from specific locations

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000064qX0AQ/bypass-authentication-for-specific-destinations-only-from-specific-locations
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-06T20:26:36.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 6, 2026 at 8:26 PM

Bypass authentication for specific destinations only from specific locations

Note:

Special thanks to

Mohammed Sakr

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction:

Maintaining a balance between strict security and a seamless user experience is essential for any organization. There are times when you might want to allow users at a specific office to access certain websites without being prompted to log in, while still requiring authentication for the rest of your company. Organizations often need to exempt specific URLs from authentication, but only when accessed from a trusted physical office. You might find that using the standard exemption settings in the portal does not provide the level of location-based granularity you require.

Solution:

To bypass authentication for specific destinations from specific locations, you can use a customized Proxy Auto-Configuration (PAC) file as shown below. This method allows Zscaler to identify the user's source Internet Protocol (IP) address and route the traffic accordingly. This solution requires that your PAC file is hosted by Zscaler.

Please note that Authentication Exemptions are applicable to cookie-based authentication traffic only, so Z-Tunnel 1.0 or 2.0 traffic is not affected by this configuration. Also, Authentication Exemptions in the Advanced Settings menu are tenant-wide and cannot be configured per location.

PAC file customization:

var egressip = "${SRCIP}";

if (shExpMatch(egressip, "203.0.113.10")) {

if (shExpMatch(url, "*.example.com")){

return "PROXY ${GATEWAY}:9480; PROXY ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:9480; DIRECT";

Here, when the user downloads the PAC file, Zscaler will return their public IP in the

egressip variable

. We can then use the public IP to check if the user belongs to the specific location from which we want to bypass authentication. Later, we can send the traffic to port 9480 to bypass authentication.

Note that as per the following documentation, authentication for 9480 traffic is bypassed only from known locations. Hence, Road Warriors are not affected by this configuration.

Documentation link:

Exempting URLs and Cloud Apps from authentication

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

## Zscaler-Microsoft Interoperability Guidance

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000065g90AA/zscalermicrosoft-interoperability-guidance
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-24T14:25:52.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Fff

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 24, 2026 at 2:25 PM

Zscaler-Microsoft Interoperability Guidance

Note:

Special thanks to

Yeicol Corrales

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

This article provides a list of domains that require a Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) bypass or a Proxy Auto-Configuration (PAC) bypass within Zscaler to ensure Microsoft applications work correctly. Bypassing these domains is necessary for Microsoft login, token issuance, Single Sign-On (SSO), device authentication, Certificate Revocation List (CRL) checks, and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) checks.

Users might experience the following issues when Zscaler performs SSL inspection on specific Microsoft authentication traffic:

Failure to sign in to Microsoft 365 applications or Teams.

Problems with modern authentication flows or token issuance.

Seamless Single Sign-On (SSO) failures.

Errors during device registration or Workplace Join.

WebView2 sign-in windows failing to load or authenticate.

Solution

To resolve these issues, you must configure your Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) SSL Inspection policy and your PAC file to bypass the following domains.

Configuring bypasses for core authentication and SSO

These URLs are essential for user login, OAuth flows, and device authentication. Add these domains to your bypass lists:

Category

Required Domains

Core Authentication and SSO

*.microsoftonline.com

*.msauth.net

*.msftauth.net

*.live.com

(Used by Office apps for consumer auth)

*.microsoft.com

login.microsoft.com

login.windows.net

Identity and Registration

autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com

(Seamless SSO)

enterpriseregistration.windows.net

(Workplace Join and device registration)

*.webview.microsoft.com

*.webview2cdn.microsoft.com

*.azure.com

*.msocsp.com (Used for OCSP responder checks)

Note

: Ensure these domains are also allowed in your firewall filtering policies to prevent connection drops.

For more detailed information on configuring these connectors, you can review the

Microsoft guide for Entra Private Access

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

Zybertech

(Customer)

1 month ago

Just wondering about the direct impact this bypass guidance has on how much Microsoft traffic Zscaler can actually inspect.

While some of the authentication URL bypasses may make sense, what about broader URLs such as login.

microsoftonline.com

? Would bypassing these prevent even basic tenancy restriction features in Zscaler?

Another example is the Microsoft‑recommended One Click Configuration for Microsoft 365. I assume the intent of this approach was to avoid large, broad domain bypasses that reduce visibility, and instead apply only the required bypasses to ensure optimisation is handled correctly.

If we follow this guidance, do we effectively lose a lot all of that visibility? In that case, any recommended controls for Microsoft traffic.

Corrales9602

(Customer)

1 month ago

Thank you for sharing your concerns here!

Certainly, bypassing all authentication URLs will assist you with issues related to certificate pinning, authentication, and various other challenges. However, utilizing the domain

microsoftonline.com

is considered a best practice when addressing application-related issues, as obtaining support from the vendor can sometimes be complex.

You may exclude domains such as

microsoftonline.com

and

microsoft.com

from your PAC file bypass, but they should not be excluded from SSL inspection.

Exempting URLs from SSL bypass does not imply that we cannot enforce policies on this specific traffic. Zscaler will extract the SNI from the connection and can implement URL filtering policies accordingly. This will enable you to manage Microsoft traffic as needed.

## Best practices for migration from SAML auto-provisioning to SCIM

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000066170AA/best-practices-for-migration-from-saml-autoprovisioning-to-scim
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-04-02T17:18:40.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited April 2, 2026 at 5:18 PM

Best practices for migration from SAML auto-provisioning to SCIM

Note:

Special thanks to

Priyanka B C

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

When users have SAML as provisioning method any changes to attributes on IDP side will not reflect immediately on the ZPA portal. The user has to reauthenticate for the changes to reflect and reauthentication could typically take hours to days.

However with SCIM based provisioning any changes to attributes will reflect instantly, therefore Zscaler always recommends using SCIM provisioning over SAML.

Solution

If you already have SAML auto-provisioning deployed and wish to migrate to SCIM , you can follow below steps to ensure a successful smooth migration:

Phase 1: Configure and enable SCIM sync:

There are two options under ZPA IDP configuration "SCIM Sync" and "SCIM Attributes for Policy".

First only enable "SCIM Sync" , perform all the required configurations on the ZPA admin portal and SCIM side.

Refer to the documentation About SCIM, Enabling SCIM for Identity Management, SCIM Configuration Guide for Microsoft Azure AD for more details.

Check with your IDP team for the approximate time required for users and attributes sync depending on your AD size. It can take hours to weeks.

Phase 2: Validate successful sync:

Once the sync is complete, navigate to Administration > SCIM management on ZPA portal.

Check SCIM sync logs , status code should be in 200 series which indicates success.

Go to "SCIM users" and "SCIM groups" tab to view the list of Users and Groups imported.

Ensure the nameId attribute imported through SAML is the same as username imported through SCIM. (SAML nameId = SCIM.user.username).

Group names imported through SCIM should exactly match the group name imported through SAML AP. Else there can be conflicts in the rule evaluation.

Phase 3: Enable SCIM attributes for Policy:

Navigate to Administration > Authentication > IDP configuration and enable the "SCIM Attributes for Policy" under respective IDP.

Adjust your policies to ensure SCIM attributes are leveraged as criteria where needed. If using SAML and SCIM in parallel, use OR logic so either source satisfies the rule until SCIM is fully validated. If this migration involves moving to different IDP refer to the documentation Migrating to new IDP configuration for more details.

Note

: At this point, both “SCIM Attributes for Policy” and “SAML Attributes for Policy” are enabled. This does not disrupt existing policies or ongoing sessions; however, it is important to confirm that SCIM‑based policy evaluations are working as expected before proceeding.

Once the option is enabled all users mapped to this IDP will be forced to reauthenticate.

The reauthentication process will not impact ongoing connections to applications or the ability to use SAML as a criteria in ZPA policies.

Phase 4 : Disable SAML attributes for Policy:

You need not disable "SAML Attributes for Policy" immediately after enabling SCIM attributes. You can use both SAML attributes and SCIM attributes in parallel.

Check as how the Access Policy is configured when you are using SAML and SCIM simultaneously.

If you have any access policies with "SAML and SCIM attributes" as a criteria for the policy , use "OR" operation so that both SAML and SCIM attributes are used. Refer to the the documentation Configuring Access Policies for more details.

Once you make sure SCIM attributes and policies are working as expected you are safe to disable SAML.

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

## How to add Management IP for NSS on Nutanix

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000066U90AI/how-to-add-management-ip-for-nss-on-nutanix
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-04-28T13:58:55.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited April 28, 2026 at 1:58 PM

How to add Management IP for NSS on Nutanix

Note:

Special thanks to

Abhishek Kumar

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

When you deploy the NSS on a Nutanix platform, the VM attempts to request an IP address via DHCP for its management interface. If a DHCP server is not available or if your network policy requires static assignments for management traffic, the NSS fails to establish network connectivity and cannot stream logs. The default configuration for the Nutanix deployment of the NSS software assumes a DHCP-enabled environment. In environments where management VLANs require static IP addresses, the default system settings must be overridden.

Solution

Configuring the management interface

Use these commands to set the IP address and default gateway immediately.

Note: These manual settings are temporary and will be lost if the VM restarts.

Log in to the Nutanix VM console.

Assign the static IP address and subnet mask to the management interface:

sudo ifconfig vtnet0 inet / up

For example: sudo ifconfig vtnet0 inet 10.1.152.93/22 up

Add the default gateway:

sudo route add default

For example: sudo route add default 10.1.151.1

Making the configuration persistent

To ensure the NSS maintains its static IP address after a reboot, you must edit the

/etc/rc.conf

file.

Open the

/etc/rc.conf

file using a text editor.

Locate the line related to DHCP for the vtnet0 interface. Comment it out by adding a hash symbol (#) at the beginning of the line:

# ifconfig_vtnet0="SYNCDHCP mtu 1460"

Add the following lines to the file, replacing the placeholders with your specific IP address and gateway:

ifconfig_vtnet0="/"

defaultrouter=""

Save the changes.

Note

: Double-check your network values before saving to ensure you do not lose connectivity to the VM.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

Note:

Special thanks to

Chetan Ramesh

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

To help troubleshoot network connections, you might need to run a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) trace. Before you begin the trace, you must complete a brief setup on your Windows machine.

Solution

Setting up your Windows machine

To prepare your machine for the trace, complete the following tasks:

Download the

WinPcap library

and install it. Note: Many machines already have WinPcap installed. If the library is already installed on your machine, proceed to the next step. Link -

https://www.winpcap.org/

Download the

tracetcp utility

. Link -

https://github.com/0xcafed00d/tracetcp/releases

Running the trace

When the required files are downloaded, complete the following steps to run the trace:

Extract the files: Unzip the downloaded folder to a convenient location.

Open Command Prompt: Launch the Command Prompt (CMD) and navigate to the directory where you extracted the files.

Execute the command: Run the following command to initiate the TCP trace to your destination:

tracetcp (domain/IP address):(port number)

Below are further options that can be used while doing a trace:

## The criteria Zscaler uses to identify which browser is handling specific traffic

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006C890AE/the-criteria-zscaler-uses-to-identify-which-browser-is-handling-specific-traffic
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-06-03T18:33:38.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited June 3, 2026 at 6:33 PM

The criteria Zscaler uses to identify which browser is handling specific traffic

Note:

Special thanks to

Mario Montero

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

Zscaler uses the

User-Agent

string included in the header section of the browser's

GET

request to enforce traffic. The

User-Agent

string contains information about the browser and operating system, which the destination server can use to tailor content accordingly.

Additionally, Zscaler uses the

sec-ch-ua

field. This is a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) header that provides details about the browser brand and version in use. This field is part of the User-Agent Client Hints.

Reviewing a debug extract

Here is a debug extract from a test environment:

GET /pagead/conversion/1052677307/?random=

Host:

www.googleadservices.com

Connection: keep-alive

sec-ch-ua-platform: "Windows"

User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/140.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

sec-ch-ua: "Chromium";v="140", "Not=A?Brand";v="24", "Google Chrome";v="140"

sec-ch-ua-mobile: ?0

As shown in the extract, Zscaler uses both the

sec-ch-ua

and

User-Agent

fields to enforce policy for the traffic.

Understanding universal

User-Agent

data

The

User-Agent

field contains universal data that is standard for all popular browsers. The User-Agent string contains browser and system information for the destination server to read.

For example, here is a sample

User-Agent

for Opera:

(Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/51.0.2704.106 Safari/537.36 OPR/38.0.2220.41)

The Opera browser is based on the Blink engine. Because of this, it looks almost identical to the Chrome User-Agent string but adds "

OPR/

". Even if you see multiple browsers listed in the

User-Agent

string, look at the last field, such as

OPR/38.0.2220.41

, to identify the correct browser.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

## Determine user count & peak transactions for an NSS virtual appliance deployment

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006C9l0AE/determine-user-count-peak-transactions-for-an-nss-virtual-appliance-deployment

Guide Details

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited June 3, 2026 at 6:45 PM

Determine user count & peak transactions for an NSS virtual appliance deployment

Note:

Special thanks to

Yeicol Corrales

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

When you deploy a new Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) virtual appliance (VA), Zscaler requests the number of users and peak transactions per hour. Providing these parameters ensures that the system provisions the image with the adequate resources required for your specific environment.

Solution

In order for the system to provision the image with adequate resources required for your specific environment, the following parameters are needed.

Determining the number of users

To obtain the total number of users in your tenant, use the Zscaler Internet Access™ (ZIA™) Admin Portal:

Go to Administration > User Management > Users.

From this page, download the CSV file.

Review the file to see the total number of users, along with their groups, departments, and status.

Determining peak transactions per hour

To calculate the peak transactions reached in ZIA

Go to Analytics > Web Insights or Firewall Insights.

Set the Time filter to Previous Days.

Set the Chart Type to Line.

Set the Units to Transactions.

Review the chart to identify the peak number of transactions reached during the previous day.

Note

: In the example provided in the portal, you might see that approximately 17 million transactions were reached at the peak. This data helps determine the necessary capacity for your deployment.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

## How to validate if a Zscaler VM is Running ZSOS24 needs redeployment

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006QCj0AM/how-to-validate-if-a-zscaler-vm-is-running-zsos24-needs-redeployment
- Type: Guide

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Andres Garcia

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited July 9, 2026 at 3:11 PM

How to validate if a Zscaler VM is Running ZSOS24 needs redeployment

Introduction:

This guide provides instructions on how to validate whether Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS), ZIA Virtual Service Edges (VSE), Data Loss Prevention Incident Receiver, Index Tool and Authentication Bridge Virtual appliance (s) need to be redeployed on Zscaler Operation System (ZSOS) 42

Note:

If you require help with a specific configuration, please contact your Technical Success Manager (TSM) or

Zscaler Support

For NSS, VSE and Authentication Bridge

Customers can quickly validate whether their NSS, VSE and Authentication Bridge are running on a RAM disk and need to redeploy appliances by using the df -hT command.

Validation Steps

Log in to the server via SSH.

Run the following command:

df -hT

Review the mount point information in the output.

Expected Result

If the filesystem is mounted on md0, the server is running on a RAM disk, and you should follow the appropriate redeployment article for that server type.

If the filesystem is not mounted on md0, the server is not running on a RAM disk, and no action is required.

For Index Tool and Incident Receiver

Customers can quickly validate whether their Index Tool and Incident Receivers are running on ZSOS42 and need to redeploy appliances by using the uname -a command.

Validation Steps

Log in to the server via SSH.

Run the following command:

uname -a

If the command shows

ZscalerOS 24-RELEASE

, the Index Tool and Incident Receiver need to be redeployed.

ZscalerOS 10.66.45.74 24-RELEASE-p4 ZscalerOS 24-RELEASE-p4 #28: Wed Feb 17 17:40:17 PST 2021   root@zero:/usr/obj/usr/src/sys/SMKERNEL amd6

Redeployment articles:

Nanolog Streaming Service

Virtual Service Edges

Index Tool

Incident Receiver

Authentication bridge

## Redeploying Authentication Bridge on ZscalerOS42

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006QpR0AU/redeploying-authentication-bridge-on-zscaleros42
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-07-01T19:13:05.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Andres Garcia

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited July 1, 2026 at 7:13 PM

Redeploying Authentication Bridge on ZscalerOS42

Introduction

This guide provides instructions on how to redeploy your

Zscaler Authentication Bridge (ZAB)

. This process is necessary when upgrading certain Authentication Bridge appliances from Zscaler Operating System 24 (

ZSOS24

) to

ZSOS42

Step 1:

Login to Admin User Interface (UI) & Navigate to Authentication Settings > Authentication Bridges.

Step 2:

If you have 2 ZAB servers registered, log into your Active ZAB Virtual Machine (VM) and confirm that it’s healthy and active. ST (State Value as 17 indicates, it’s healthy and active.)

Step 3:

Once the above is confirmed it means this ZAB is actively serving Auth/Provisioning transactions. The secondary ZAB can be safely shut down with the command - zab stop

Step 4:

On the Admin UI, proceed to edit the secondary inactive ZAB and set the status to Disabled.

Step 5:

Confirm from the Inactive ZAB that it’s on ZSOS24 (using uname -a )

Once ZSOS24 is confirmed you can proceed to re-deploy a new VM with ZSOS42.

Step 6:

On the Admin UI, in the Authentication Bridges Page hit the Download ZAB VM, Enter the number of Users and click Compute. You will get the Download ZAB VM link that fits the user base — use it to download the OVA file. It’s recommended to keep the ZAB VM with extra memory resources (~ 16GB) to avoid any compute issues with large user bases.

Step7:

Deploy the new ZAB using the OVA file that you downloaded from the compute section.

Step 8:

Download the Secure Socket Layer (SSL) Certificate present on Admin UI against the respective listed ZAB.

Step 9:

Follow the

ZAB Configuration

steps to complete the configuration. Use the same certificate you downloaded from Admin UI for the respective ZAB.

Step 10:

After the configuration is complete, toggle the status to Enabled for the ZAB that was previously Disabled.

Step 11:

Once the ZAB is restarted, it will connect back to the Zscaler Cloud as listed in the help document ( sockstat -4 ). It will take a few minutes for the ZAB to refresh all the objects in memory.

Step 12:

Ensure your On-prem Domain Name System (DNS) points to correct hostname/IP address as configured in Advanced Configuration of Active Directory in Authentication Settings.

Step 13:

Once this is complete, repeat the same steps for the Active ZAB and the secondary ZAB will automatically take over as Primary and have the state as 17.

Note:

If you only have one ZAB active currently, then deploy a secondary ZAB directly using the ZSOS42 OVA image using the steps mentioned in the

help documentation

Step 1:

Ensure your On-prem DNS points to correct hostname/IP address as configured in Advanced Configuration of Active Directory in Authentication Settings.

Step 2:

Once it’s deployed, set the status as Enabled for the new secondary ZAB and toggle the status of current Primary ZAB as Disabled.

Step 3:

After a few minutes, the new ZAB will take over as the primary ZAB, and the old ZAB VM on Admin UI can be deleted and the old VM can be safely decommissioned.

## DNS cache poisoning and DNSSEC

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evkf9CAA/dns-cache-poisoning-and-dnssec
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-07-06T11:44:34.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Stefan Sebastian

(Employee) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

Edited by sfdc July 6, 2023 at 11:44 AM

DNS cache poisoning and DNSSEC

The Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR) clusters located in each data center along with the DNS Control capability of Advanced Cloud Firewall resist DNS poisoning is two main ways:

If the customer chooses to DNAT route (and redirect) DNS traffic to our Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR) then we use DNSSEC on the backend for our iterative resolutions. This verifies the authoritative server and domain response when the external authoritative DNS supports. Not all authoritative DNS servers support DNSSEC but the ZTR will always try DNSSEC first. It will do this in an iterative manner and so, for example, get the key for root, then the TLD etc.

Regardless of whether our ZTR is used or some 3rd party public DNS is used, DNS Control will check the domain and the IP response for indications that the IP is used for malicious purposes or is categorized in a category that the customer does not want. This will eliminate some bad DNS responses (particularly the “Malicious? category) looking to poison the end user’s cache and detect caches that are poisoned.

We typically hold DNS records in the local cache per data center for the TTL duration.

The diagram below shows both where DNSSEC is employed and the resolver versus transit options enabled by Destination NAT configuration rules in the Firewall Filtering section of the UI console:
